pillars.name: Line
pillars.summary: The one protocol every Agent, server and browser speaks.
pillars.description: Line (Logically Interconnected Neural-Engine) is how Agents reach the server and each other. Every hop is sealed, and Agent-to-Agent traffic is sealed end to end, so the server relays what it cannot read. It is one frame envelope with request and reply, per-capability flow control and guaranteed delivery, and it builds under TinyGo, so the same Agent code runs in a browser. Everything else on this roadmap travels over it.

pillars.name: Mesh
pillars.summary: The Agents a customer runs, one mode each, and what each one is for.
pillars.description: The Mesh is the customer's own Agents. One binary runs in one of several modes, and each mode is a job with its own tools: filter DNS, proxy package installs, enforce an editor policy, steward a database. Agents run on the customer's machines, in their cluster or in a browser tab, and they do the org's work against the outside world, so the server never holds the org's credentials. Every Mesh item is one mode.

pillars.name: Armory
pillars.summary: Armornet's threat intelligence and research, from listening for threats to a verdict on a package or vendor.
pillars.description: The Armory is the machine-learning and AI analysis of the software supply chain, run by research Agents at scale. It listens: threat feeds, forks of the projects customers depend on, and new versions of their dependencies. It judges: suspicious packages run in a sandbox and get a multi-model verdict. And it publishes what it finds as indicators every Agent enforces. Customers meet it through Vendor Intelligence, Package Monitoring and Sandbox review; the research network under them is worked on the whole time.

pillars.name: Open source: products
pillars.summary: The packages Armornet publishes under Apache 2.0, one item each.
pillars.description: The first release open-sources everything Armornet is built on, so each published package is a product in its own right: Showcase (with Breach), the Identity Library, the Database Manager and the OTA updater. Each is its own module with no armornet imports, published by git subtree. Net-new work is allowed here before 1.0. The relay proxies and the network stay closed.

pillars.name: Open source: initiatives
pillars.summary: Work Armornet does for the open-source projects it and its customers depend on.
pillars.description: Open source is how Armornet earns trust with the communities it depends on: real, free work that helps maintainers keep up, not only work that benefits Armornet. The Armory already watches these projects; these initiatives turn what it sees into contributions. A person always reviews and opens anything that reaches upstream.

pillars.name: Engine
pillars.summary: The console workflows and rollout that bind the pillars together.
pillars.description: Product work that is no Agent mode, no Armory research and no published package: getting Agents onto every machine, and the console workflows a security team runs day to day, such as risk, controls, policies and documents. These are what a buyer sees in a demo, and most of them read what the Mesh and the Armory produce.
